subject: Post-call: model fit & Redwood benchmarks for Acme Retail
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Cc: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai

Subject: Post-call: model fit & Redwood benchmarks for Acme Retail

Hi Lisa / Raj — great to speak today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Summary of needs:
- Primary use case: personalized product descriptions + short in-app recommendations (concise, factual).
- Data constraints: PII redaction required; all inference must be isolated per-account for EU customers.
- Traffic profile: bursty e-commerce traffic with estimated peak ~200 requests/sec (128-token avg).
- Quality bar: human-level fluency on product copy; minimize hallucinations on attributes.
- Latency SLO: target p50 <= 200ms, p95 <= 500ms for 1–2 token streaming responses.

What I’m sharing (attached and links below):
- Redwood-verified performance profiles (TPS, latency percentiles) for candidate models.
- A starter prompt set (attached CSV) based on today’s sample prompts to validate quality/regression.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll send recommended model variants (latency vs. quality tradeoffs) and Redwood benchmark links.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra and data team (30–45m) to review integration, batching, and KV-cache options.
3) You provide a small blinded evaluation set (up to 500 examples) and any IP restrictions for our evaluation sandbox.

Attachments: redwood_verified_performance_profiles_20260225.pdf, acme_prompt_set_v1.csv

If this looks right, can we target a technical deep-dive next week (options: Wed 3/3 or Thu 3/4)?

Sincerely,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

- Can you highlight which models you recommend for our mix (throughput-heavy vs. higher-fidelity)?
- Are the benchmark numbers per-request (128-token avg) or token/sec? We want to understand TPS vs. token throughput.
- We’re concerned about quality regressions after model updates — how does Redwood detect and alert on regressions tied to prompt sets/evals?

We can do Wed 3/3 in the morning PT — Raj and I will aim for that slot but please confirm.

VP, Personalization | Acme Retail
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acmeretail.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@acmeretail.com>
Cc: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-27T11:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & Redwood benchmarks for Acme Retail

Lisa — great questions. Below is a concise recommendation and what the attached benchmark artifacts mean. I’ve included TPS and latency percentiles (measured at 128-token avg, requests/sec). Full profiles and raw traces are linked in the dashboard.

Recommended model variants (tradeoffs):
- redwood-llm-7B-q4 (quantized): Balanced option. Expected throughput: ~180–220 req/s (128-token avg) on our standard mGPUs; latency p50 ~160ms, p95 ~420ms, p99 ~620ms. Good balance of generation quality and cost; recommended starting point.
- redwood-llm-13B-static: Higher quality for tricky attribute preservation. Throughput ~70–90 req/s; latency p50 ~220ms, p95 ~600ms. Use for A/B samples where higher fidelity is required.
- redwood-small-int8: Lower-cost, high-TPS option for shallow rewriting tasks (templates). Throughput ~400+ req/s; latency p50 ~90ms, p95 ~260ms. Expect lower open-ended generation quality vs. 7B/13B.

Notes on benchmarks and measurements:
- TPS = requests/sec at 128-token average. Our dashboard includes separate token/sec numbers and CPU/GPU utilization traces.
- Latency percentiles in the profiles are end-to-end (model inference only) measured under representative e-commerce burst patterns with adaptive batching.
- The attached PDF (redwood_verified_performance_profiles_20260225.pdf) contains per-model percentile tables and the config used to reproduce the runs. Link: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-retail-2026

Quality regression & evals:
- Recommended approach: add your 300–500 blinded examples to a private eval set in Redwood Optimize. We’ll run weekly baseline and delta checks on exact-match, ROUGE, and a small human-rated quality rubric.
- Regression alerts: Redwood can trigger alerts when model-level metrics degrade beyond a threshold (configurable) on the evaluation prompt set. We also support automatic canary rollbacks to a pinned model if production degrade is detected.
- Prompt-stability: we’ll run a prompt-perturbation suite from the attached CSV to validate robustness across phrasing.

Next steps / asks from Acme:
1) Share the 300–500 eval examples (can be anonymized).
2) Confirm which model(s) you want us to include in an A/B run (I suggest 7B-q4 vs small-int8 for cost/latency experiments).
3) Confirm Wed 3/3 10:00am PT for the technical deep-dive — I’ll include our infra and reliability engineer.

I’m attaching the starter prompt set again (acme_prompt_set_v1.csv) and the verified performance PDF. Also linking the perf-profiles page: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/perf-profiles/model-catalog#gpt-like-quantized

CC’ing Aisha (solutions engineer) and Marissa (CS lead) so they can prep the evaluation harness and an infra playbook for the deep-dive.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acmeretail.com>

One more ask: can Marissa include a short runbook on how Redwood flags regressions during a canary rollout? We’ll need that for our procurement/security review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround on the benchmark artifacts — sharing the perf dashboard link with our infra folks now.

Best,
Lisa
